overall: The AG found the Hubbardston Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: fewer than a quorum was present for the post-Selectmen-meeting conversation, and the untrue-comments allegation was declined as not an OML issue.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a noticed meeting after attending a Board of Selectmen meeting on February 27, 2017.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board did not deliberate outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Whether the post-Selectmen-meeting conversation among Board members was deliberation, given that only two of three attending members were present for most of it.
allegations.key_passage: Because Mr. Robinson was outside the meeting room for much of the conversation, there was less than a quorum present.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; the AG noted the Board's notice listing only 'Attend Board of Selectmen's meeting' lacked topic detail.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the notice stated that the Board would attend the Board of Selectmen meeting, but it provided no information as to what matters the Board anticipated discussing.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board made negative and untrue comments about the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
